subject: general
question: One carbon credit contains:
solution:
The correct answer is __**1000 kg of carbon dioxide**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• One carbon credit is equivalent to the reduction or removal of **1000 kg of carbon dioxide** from the atmosphere.
 
• Carbon credits are part of international attempts to mitigate the growth in concentrations of greenhouse gases (GHGs).
 
• They provide a way to reduce greenhouse gas emissions on an industrial scale by capping total annual emissions and letting the market assign a monetary value to any shortfall through trading.
 
• Organizations or countries with higher emissions can purchase carbon credits to comply with the emission limits set by regulatory bodies.
 
• This system incentivizes the reduction of carbon emissions and promotes the use of cleaner technologies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Carbon credits are often traded in carbon markets, which can be either compliance markets or voluntary markets.
 
• Compliance markets are created and regulated by mandatory national, regional, or international carbon reduction regimes.
 
• Voluntary markets, on the other hand, allow entities to purchase carbon credits on a voluntary basis to offset their own emissions.
 
• The concept of carbon credits originated from the Kyoto Protocol, an international treaty that commits its parties by setting internationally binding emission reduction targets.
